name: Probability and Statistics
topics: Probability, Conditional Probability and Bayes' Theorem
Boxes A, B, C, D contain fuses with given defect rates. A fuse selected at random is defective; find the probability that it came from box D.
Prove that if A and B are independent then A and B' are also independent; solve the given problem on alternate throws of dice.
Descriptive Statistics: Mean, Median, Mode, Dispersion, Moments
Calculate the mean, median and mode of the given frequency distribution, and the standard deviation and coefficient of variation.
Calculate the first four moments about the mean and hence β₁ and β₂; find moments about the mean from moments about a point.
Random Variables, PMF/PDF and CDF
A random variable X has the given probability distribution. Find k, the required probabilities and the smallest value of x for which P(X ≤ x) > 1/2.
Find the constant and the cumulative distribution function of the given density, and the distribution of Y = g(X).
Expectation, Variance and Covariance
Find E[2X − 3Y + 7] and Var[2X − 3Y + 7] for independent X and Y with the given moments.
Prove that Cov(aX + b, cY + d) = ac·Cov(X, Y), and find the covariance between X + Y and X − Y.
Moment Generating Functions
Derive the moment generating function of the Poisson / normal / exponential distribution and find its mean and variance.
Prove that the MGF of a sum of independent random variables equals the product of their MGFs; find the MGF of Y = aX + b.
Joint, Marginal and Conditional Distributions
For the given joint pdf, find the constant c, the marginal density of X and the conditional density of Y given X.
Three balls are drawn without replacement from a box; find the joint probability distribution of the numbers of white and red balls drawn.
Discrete Distributions: Binomial, Poisson, Geometric
Out of 800 families with 4 children, how many are expected to have 2 boys and 2 girls, no girl, at most 2 girls?
Power failures follow a Poisson distribution with a given average; find the probability of at most one failure in a week.
Continuous Distributions: Normal, Exponential, Uniform and CLT
The resistance of resistors is normal with mean 100 Ω and SD 2 Ω; what percentage lie between 98 and 102 Ω?
A part's lifetime is exponentially distributed with mean 10 years; find the probability it lasts between 9 and 11 years. State the central limit theorem.
Correlation and Regression
Estimate the regression line of Y on X from the given data and predict Y for the given X.
Compute the rank correlation coefficient; prove that if one regression coefficient exceeds unity the other must be less than unity.
Hypothesis Testing: Large Samples (Z-test)
Is there a significant difference between the proportions favouring a plan in two cities at 5% level?
Explain null and alternative hypotheses, critical region, Type I and II errors, and one-tailed vs two-tailed tests.
Small Sample Tests: t-test and F-test
Test whether the given sample of 9 items differs significantly from an assumed mean of 47.5.
Two independent samples are given; test whether their means/variances differ significantly at 5% level.
Chi-Square Test
Test whether the production of bad parts is independent of the shift at 5% level using the chi-square test.
In 120 throws of a die the given frequencies were observed. Can the die be regarded as biased?
